summary: A first-person excerpt from a novel (Book 1, part 97) in which the narrator, hungover after a late-night flirtation with Ange, wanders the Mission district on a Saturday. He notices graffiti, including the slogan DON'T TRUST ANYONE OVER 25, and learns through anonymous Xnet blogs that a movement and a park concert by that name have been planned for weeks. He also reflects on his estrangement from Van, Jolu and Darryl, and ends by deciding to revisit an anarchist bookstore.
one_line: A narrator in San Francisco's Mission district discovers an Xnet-organized park concert and anti-authority graffiti movement called Don't Trust Anyone Over 25.
key_facts: The narrator recalls a poster in the Mission of old revolutionary Emma Goldman with the caption "If I can't dance, I don't want to be a part of your revolution."
The narrator had been spending his energies figuring out how to use the Xnet to organize dedicated fighters so they could jam the DHS.
The narrator and Ange chatted and flirted until 4AM, and the following day he was a zombie from a hangover and sleep deprivation.
The excerpt takes place on a Saturday, and the narrator gets up around lunchtime to head out onto the streets.
The narrator notes that the Mission's taggers kept going under the nose of the DHS, and that some cameras had been spray-painted over.
Painted in ten-foot-high letters on the side of an auto-yard's fence were the words DON'T TRUST ANYONE OVER 25.
The narrator wonders whether someone who left his "party" the night before came to paint the slogan.
The narrator says Van is not talking to him, he is not ready to talk to Jolu, and he cannot call Darryl.
The narrator describes anonablogs on the Xnet as untraceable to any author unless the author puts her name on it.
Plans for the concert in the park had been circulating for weeks, hopping from blog to blog and becoming a full-blown movement.
The concert is called Don't Trust Anyone Over 25, and the narrator realizes this explains where Ange got the slogan.
On Monday morning the narrator decides he wants to check out the anarchist bookstore again.
